headline: Motion to approve draft horseback permit for Casavant meadow failed 0-4; members elected new officers.
summary: The commission discussed a draft permit for horse carriage rides in Casavant's meadow, which would not extend to city streets. Speakers raised questions about costs, park use, and fees. Members elected Carly Schneider chair, Meredith Bushey vice chair, and Dana Howe secretary.
decisions: Failed 0-4 a motion to approve the draft horseback permit and move it forward to City Council.
Tabled approval of previous meeting minutes to a future meeting.
Tabled the City of Winooski commission structure discussion to a future meeting.
Approved Carly Schneider as chair, passed unanimously.
Approved Meredith Bushey as vice chair, passed unanimously.
Approved Dana Howe as secretary, passed unanimously.

11/10/2026 - Minutes
Call to Order
Names (First and Last) of Members Present: Dana Howe, Carly Schneider, Courtney Blasius, 
Meredith Bushey
Name of City Council Liaison Present: Deputy Mayor Bryn Oakleaf
Name of Staff Liaison Present: Ray Coffey, Justin Huizenga
Names of Guests (First and Last) Present: Harly Rodriguez (I&B Commissioner), Alissa 
Johnson, Alex Giruleu, Gwen Heaghney, Kate Coffey, Jean Szilva, Sarah van Ryckevorsel, Dr. 
Ron Stotyn, Bridget Ahrens
Call to Order by: Dana Howe
Meeting Start Time: 5:33 PM
Minutes Recorded by: Ray Coffey
Public Comment
While there was no initial public comment, the committee recommended moving item V as the 
first item to discuss. Motion to approve the changes to the agenda were unanimous.
Approve Previous Meeting Minutes
This item was tabled for a future meeting.
Discussion: City of Winooski Commission Structure
This item was tabled for a future meeting.
Discussion/Approval: Draft Horseback Permit
The Community Services Director gave an overview of the history, process previously 
established, and summary of the permit. A little over a year ago, the developer for the new Sugar 
House Hotel had interest in offering horse carriage rides seasonally in the winter with a sleigh 
and wheeled carts during the summer for hotel patrons and possibly community members. This 
would not be an everyday offering, but approximately a dozen times a year. The city ordinance at 
the time of the request did not allow horseback riding so city staff were asked to bring language 
forward to the city council last December. The Council made the recommendation to change 
the ordinance to allow horseback riding and/or horseback activity by written permit. With the 
ordinance language change, it did not allow for immediate action to occur but allowed an option 
for staff and council to move forward with continued work on this process. The Community 
Services Director needs to ensure the application process, rules, regulations, and guidelines are 
clearly established before any possible next steps. The draft permit application was presented to 
the commission for feedback.
The Commission could recommend sending the permit application to council or not. The 
Community Services Director reminded the Commission that as an advisory board, they do not 
have decision making authority, but act as advisory for council to make further decisions.
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf commented that even though the change in the ordinance is in place, the 
process by which a permit can be applied for, reviewed, and approved does not exist yet. This 
conversation is for establishing a process.
Dr. Ron Stotyn, who used to be a former chair of a previous iteration of this commission, gave 
comments about previous intentions relating to the Casavant natural area being a place for 
pedestrians specifically so they can enjoy the flora and fauna with the least possible risk to 
interfering with the land.
Bridget Ahrens asked questions about updating the terrain and costs associated with the 
project. Ray responded by giving information about the trail modification process and made 
mention that these proposed activities would be permitted for the meadow area of the park 
specifically. The city and the developer split the cost of wetland delineation; the meadow is 
outside of the wetlands buffer. In addition, proposed horse trails would not be extended into other 
parts of the park. Access to the park was altered due to the hotel development, and the hotel 
built a truck graded bridge which has the capacity to take emergency vehicles in and out of the 
park, and they are working on wetland restoration around the bridge project. Regarding cost, 
nothing is outlined in the capital budget, and the Community Services Department is seeking 
grant funding and match dollar amounts from the developer if this project is to move forward.
After public comments, Ray outlined the next steps, and circled back to the permit application. 
Section one clarifies that this is specifically for Casavant’s meadow and not on city streets. 
Discussion ensued amongst the Commission members related to proposed activities and 
clarification of language.
Continued public comments on behalf of Sarah van Ryckevorsel were shared regarding using 
public park space for a project like this would only be beneficial if there was a big fee amount for 
the city to collect as well as ensuring that it would an affordable service for all.
Discussion continued amongst the Commission regarding broadness in the permit as well as 
their comfortability with the overall policy and questioning who and what benefits from something 
like this.
Additional public comment was made regarding an appreciation of the initial steps taken and the 
work the city has put into making this application.
The Deputy Mayor outlined next steps for this item’s consideration and asked for a motion to be 
made on behalf of the Commission.
Motion to approve the permit and move forward the discussion to City Council made by Dana 
Howe and seconded by Courtney Blasius.
Motion failed 0-4.
Approval: Election of Commission Officers (Chair, Vice Chair, Secretary)
The Community Services Director gave an overview of the commission structure, officer roles 
and responsibilities, as related to the advisory group. Discussion ensued amongst the group 
about current members’ roles and desires. There is still one seat as well as two alternate 
positions available as well.
Motion to approve Carly as chair made by Courtney Blasius and seconded by Dana Howe. 
Motion passed unanimously.
Motion to approve Meredith as vice chair made by Courtney Blasius and seconded by Dana 
Howe. Motion passed unanimously.
Motion to approve Dana as secretary made by Meredith Bushey and seconded by Courtney 
Blasius. Motion passed unanimously.
Inclusion and Belonging Commission Liaison Updates
The commission was unable to meet for their last meeting and has a meeting planned towards 
the end of this month. There was a recent new appointment to the commission and there are 
three more candidates for review.
City Council and City Staff Liaison Updates
Deputy Mayor Oakleaf commented that before the next City Council meeting on December 7th
that Downtown Winooski will host the craft market in the rotary. In addition, the farmers market 
this this Sunday, November 15, from 10-1. In addition, the Winooski School District is hosting a 
craft fair on Saturday, November 21.
Ray started his updates stating the library had their busiest October ever. Ray also shared his 
appreciation with everyone involved in the Halloween celebration. In addition, the Community 
Services Department is working on developing summer programs and registration sign-ups will 
begin February 1st. Lastly, budget planning starts in December and the first meeting with City 
Council is on Monday, December 7th. Community Services will be presenting to Council on 
January 4, 2027.
Other Business
None
Adjourn
Motion by: Meredith Bushey
Second: Dana Howe
Meeting End Time: 7:06 PM
